ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

An estrogen interaction

A patient with well-controlled epilepsy takes lamotrigine and an estrogen-containing contraceptive. She plans to stop the contraceptive and asks whether this can affect her seizure medication. Which change should the prescriber anticipate and monitor?

  1. No possible pharmacokinetic effect
  2. An increase in lamotrigine exposure
  3. Complete loss of lamotrigine absorption
  4. An obligatory fall in lamotrigine concentration
  5. Conversion of lamotrigine into an inactive prodrug
Answer and explanation

An increase in lamotrigine exposure

Estrogen-containing contraceptives increase lamotrigine clearance; stopping estrogen can raise lamotrigine levels.

Option explanations

An increase in lamotrigine exposure: Estrogen-containing contraceptives increase lamotrigine clearance; stopping estrogen can raise lamotrigine levels.

Complete loss of lamotrigine absorption: Stopping estrogen does not abolish absorption.

An obligatory fall in lamotrigine concentration: The expected direction after stopping estrogen is an increase.

Conversion of lamotrigine into an inactive prodrug: The interaction concerns clearance, not prodrug conversion.

No possible pharmacokinetic effect: The estrogen interaction can require dose reassessment.
